messages:
sara: Quick question 025-01: I had to cut a client trip short for a family emergency and flew back a day early. Hotel charged a non-refundable one-night cancellation fee and issued a hotel credit voucher for the rest of the stay under my name, airline issued a flight voucher too. Can I expense the cancellation fee and what do we do with the vouchers/credits?

 tom (People Ops): So sorry to hear that 
. Policy summary: unavoidable cancellation fees tied to business travel are reimbursable with receipts and manager approval. Any travel credits/vouchers issued to the traveler are company property if the original trip was business; they should be returned to travel ops or used for future company travel. If vendor rules prevent transfer, document that.

 jules (Finance): To process: we need original booking confirmation, hotel cancellation invoice showing the fee, the voucher/credit code and terms, and your card statement line showing the charge (if paid personally). If the vendor issues a refundable credit, Finance will offset reimbursed amounts against that credit.

 sara: Hotel says vouchers must be used by the same guest name and can't be transferred. Theyre willing to apply it to a future stay only under my name.

 tom (People Ops): If vendor policy blocks transfer, two options: 1) ask vendor for refund instead of voucher, or 2) we accept the voucher as company asset — you'll schedule future company travel and apply voucher, or hand over the voucher details to travel ops. Please capture vendor policy text.

 jules (Finance): Note: if the voucher ends up being used for personal travel, that becomes a taxable fringe benefit and we need preapproval and payroll reporting. Don't use it for personal trips.

 sara: Per diem question: trip shortened by 1 night. Do I get full per diem or prorated?

 jules (Finance): Per diem follows the standard rule: first and last travel days are 50% of the daily meal rate, full days are 100%. In shortened trips, submit per diem only for the nights actually slept on business travel. If you used receipts instead of per diem for certain meals, attach those.

 sara: I paid the cancellation fee on my personal card (last 4: 9876) and got verbal OK from my manager on the phone. Is that fine?

 tom (People Ops): Manager verbal ok is acceptable if you capture it in writing afterward (Slack message or email ok). Retro approvals trigger a manual review but are allowed for emergencies. Upload the manager confirmation.

 travel-bot: Reminder: Attach booking confirmation, cancellation invoice, voucher screenshot/code, card statement line, and manager approval when you submit the expense. Missing items will delay processing.

 jules (Finance): Quick example you can paste into the expense app:

 ```
Trip: London client visit (proj-Oak)
Expense: Hotel cancellation fee (non-refundable)
Amount: GBP 120
Paid with: personal card (last 4 digits: 9876)
Manager approval: @matt (sent 2026-02-18 14:33)
Voucher: Hotel voucher code HVT-2026-3345, expires 2027-02-01, non-transferable
Notes: Trip cut short due to family emergency; vendor policy prevents voucher transfer; requesting reimbursement for cancellation fee and guidance on voucher handling.
```

 sara: Thanks 
I'll upload everything and ping travel ops.

 tom (People Ops): TL;DR checklist: 1) booking confirmation, 2) cancellation invoice, 3) voucher screenshot/code + vendor terms, 4) card statement, 5) manager approval message, 6) expense note explaining emergency. We'll mark this for manual review and coordinate voucher disposition. :white_check_mark:
